title: N'th Element of a List
semantic_obligations: The public OCaml interface is at : int -> 'a list -> 'a option.
For every nonnegative i with i < list length, return Some of the element at exactly zero-based position i.
For every nonnegative i with i >= list length, return None rather than an exception.
Selection is positional: preserve list order and distinguish duplicate occurrences by index.
The entrypoint is polymorphic in list element type and has no effects, mutation, randomness, string-specific, float-specific, or infinite-stream behavior.

source_ambiguity.evidence: The pinned statement gives only nonnegative zero-based examples and contrasts List.nth out-of-bounds failure; it never defines at (-1) xs.
source_ambiguity.treatment: Negative-index behavior is deliberately not asserted in contract.sq or test_generated.ml. This prevents inventing a benchmark semantic requirement.

required_features: Synquid abstract refinements relating a finite-list position to its element
Synquid algebraic option datatype with a payload refinement
Synquid measures for finite-list length and option constructor discrimination
Linear integer arithmetic and Boolean implications

synthesis_attempts.result: resolution error: variable _v was not in scope in the abstract-refinement parameter position
rejected: Cannot find sufficiently strong refinements when attempting the zero-index recursive branch; the attempted component environment omitted integer equality

post_attempt_contract_note: The explicit generic eq primitive was added after attempt 2 because the error identified it as missing. No third synthesis was run: the task permits at most two reasoned attempts. Therefore no candidate is claimed.

coverage: head, last, empty, and past-end cases

negative_control_evidence.observed_failure: official: index 2: expected Some <value>, got None

implementation_boundary: No final OCaml implementation was authored, copied, or mechanically lowered. A Synquid result would remain only a candidate until a backend lowers it and the independent OCaml semantic tests pass.
